title: Inequalities and absolute value
objective: Express the full solution set of a linear, compound, or absolute-value inequality with correct endpoints.
why: An engineering requirement is often a range: a temperature must stay below a limit, a resistance must lie within tolerance, or a signal must exceed a threshold. Solving an inequality tells you every acceptable input. Boundary values matter because a strict limit and an inclusive limit make different promises.

sections.heading: A solution is a set of values
paragraphs: The statement $x<3$ is true for every real number below 3. Its solution is a whole set, not the single number 3. The statement $x\le3$ also allows the boundary value 3. Read the symbols aloud: less than, less than or equal to, greater than, and greater than or equal to.

On a number line, an open circle excludes a boundary value and a filled circle includes it. Shade all allowed values. A graph's displayed window is finite, but an arrow indicates the set continues beyond that window. Infinity describes that unbounded direction; it is not an ordinary endpoint you can include.

Interval notation records the same information. Parentheses exclude endpoints and square brackets include them. For example, $(-\infty,3)$ represents $x<3$; $(-\infty,3]$ represents $x\le3$; and $[2,5)$ represents $2\le x<5$. Infinity always receives a parenthesis.

In the app, type (-inf, 3), (-inf, 3], or [2, 5). Separate disjoint intervals with U, such as (-inf, 0) U (0, inf). That last set excludes zero; it is not the same as all real numbers. Type R for the entire real line and empty for no solutions.

sections.heading: Why a negative multiplier reverses the sign
paragraphs: Adding or subtracting the same number on both sides preserves an inequality's direction. Multiplying or dividing by a positive number also preserves the direction. For example, $2x+1<7$ becomes $2x<6$, then $x<3$.

Multiplying or dividing both sides by a negative number reverses their order. Since $2<3$, multiplication by -1 gives $-2>-3$. Reflection across zero reverses which number lies farther to the right. This is why solving $-2x<6$ gives $x>-3$.

The sign reversal belongs to multiplication or division by a negative quantity. Subtracting a number does not itself reverse the sign. When the divisor contains an unknown variable, you cannot assume its sign; later lessons will use sign charts to handle that situation.

After solving, test one point inside your proposed region, one outside it, and the boundary itself. These checks catch common errors. They support the algebraic derivation; they do not replace a reason why every point in the region works.

sections.heading: AND and OR describe different combinations
paragraphs: AND means both conditions must hold. To solve $x>1$ AND $x\le4$, keep only their overlap: $(1,4]$. This is an intersection. An input of 0 fails the first condition; an input of 5 fails the second; an input of 4 satisfies both.
OR means at least one condition must hold. The statement $x<1$ OR $x\ge4$ gives $(-\infty,1)\cup[4,\infty)$. This is a union. It describes two separated regions, not the interval between 1 and 4.

Some intersections are empty. The conditions $x>5$ AND $x\le2$ cannot hold together. Some unions cover the entire real line: $x<5$ OR $x\ge2$ leaves no gap. Always consider overlap before copying two pieces into the answer.

A chained inequality such as $-2<3x+1\le7$ requires all three expressions to preserve their order. Subtract 1 from each part to get $-3<3x\le6$, then divide each part by 3 to obtain $-1<x\le2$. If dividing a chain by a negative number, reverse both inequality signs and rewrite the final bounds in increasing order.

sections.heading: Absolute value describes distance
paragraphs: The quantity $|x-h|$ is the distance from x to a center h. A distance is nonnegative. The inequality $|x-h|<r$ with $r>0$ means x is closer than r units to h, so $h-r<x<h+r$. The inclusive version uses inclusive endpoints.

For $|x-h|>r$ with $r>0$, the point must be farther than r units from h. There are two regions: $x<h-r$ OR $x>h+r$. Do not join those two conditions with AND, because no input can be simultaneously to the left of the lower boundary and to the right of the upper boundary.

Treat zero or negative thresholds directly from the meaning of distance. The inequality $|x-h|<0$ has no solutions. The inequality $|x-h|\le0$ permits only $x=h$, represented by $[h,h]$. The condition $|x-h|>0$ allows every real input except h, while $|x-h|\ge0$ allows all real inputs.

A negative threshold cannot be treated as a positive radius. For example, $|x-2|<-1$ is impossible, but $|x-2|>-1$ is always true. Check this before splitting into cases. The rule $|x|=x$ also requires $x\ge0$; when x is negative, $|x|=-x$.

sections.heading: Translate a tolerance requirement
paragraphs: Suppose a component's resistance R must be within 5 ohms of 100 ohms, including the boundary. The requirement is $|R-100|\le5$. It gives $95\le R\le105$, or $[95,105]$ ohms. Values 95 and 105 pass; 94.9 and 105.1 fail.

Words such as at most and at least include equality. Less than, greater than, and strictly within exclude the boundary. If a specification says within without stating its boundary policy, write down the interpretation being used rather than hiding the ambiguity.

A percent tolerance must be converted into an absolute distance before applying the interval formula. A 2 percent tolerance around 150 ohms is 3 ohms, so the inclusive accepted interval is $[147,153]$. The nominal value is the center; the tolerance is the radius.

A physical context can impose an additional domain. If a mathematical distance condition includes negative times but the model applies only for $t\ge0$, intersect the solution with that time domain. Keep the algebraic result and the contextual restriction visible as separate steps.

examples.title: A negative coefficient

steps.reason: Subtract 4 from both sides without reversing the inequality.
Divide by -3. Division by a negative number reverses the direction.
The comparison is strict, so -2 is excluded. Negative infinity always uses an open end.
The inside test point -3 satisfies the original inequality.
The boundary gives equality, so it does not satisfy the strict comparison.

examples.conclusion: The complete solution set is (-inf, -2). For comparison, the outside point 0 gives 4, which is not greater than 10.

examples.title: An inclusive distance requirement

steps.reason: Distance at most 3 means the signed displacement is between -3 and 3, including both boundaries.
Add 5 to every part of the chained inequality.
Both boundaries are allowed because equality was included.
Both endpoints pass the original requirement.

examples.conclusion: The solution is [2, 8]. A value such as 5 is inside the interval and has distance zero. A value such as 9 is outside and has distance four.

guided.title: Choose the correct two regions
guided.setup: Solve $|x+2|>4$. The center is -2 because $x+2=x-(-2)$. The two boundary points are -6 and 2.
before: The distance must be greater than 4, so select the outside regions.
The comparison is strict, so exclude each boundary. Use U to combine the two regions.

hints: Farther away means outside the interval between the boundary points.
One region lies below -6. The other lies above 2.
explanation: Subtracting 2 gives $x<-6$ OR $x>2$. Neither boundary is included.

guided.after: An answer containing only one of the two regions misses valid inputs. Check one point on each side, such as -7 and 3.

interaction.prompt: Predict the entire solution set, then reveal the number line. Change the center, threshold, and comparison. Explore a strict boundary, a zero threshold, and a negative threshold, and explain each result using distance.

summary: An inequality describes a complete set of inputs, including decisions about its boundaries.
Reverse the inequality after multiplication or division by a negative value; ordinary addition or subtraction does not reverse it.
AND takes the overlap. OR takes the union. Consider empty sets and overlapping regions.
Absolute value is distance: smaller distances usually give an inside interval and larger distances give two outside regions.
Zero and negative thresholds need direct interpretation. State any physical domain and units.
retrieval: Explain why dividing by a negative reverses an inequality. Then solve one inclusive tolerance condition and one strict outside-distance condition without looking at the examples.
